Subject: Salary scale translation and localization rules — global bands -> local offers

Hi all,

Following our comp working group, attached is a proposed methodology to translate Redwood's global compensation bands into localized offer bands for EMEA markets. The goal is to create repeatable conversion rules so recruiters and hiring managers have deterministic offer guidance. Please review the attached spreadsheet ("2027-Q4-bands-translation-v2.xlsx") and the MarketScout benchmarking packet I shared with the market data.

Key asks:
- Agree on a mapping rule (e.g., global band midpoint -> local median percentile, rounding rules).
- Confirm which elements are preserved vs. re-denominated (base salary, target OTE, signing bonus guardrails).
- Decide regional uplifts (APAC/EMEA) and whether to apply country-level modifiers for London/Berlin/Zurich.
- Approve the sign-off workflow: hiring manager -> People Partner -> Compensation Lead -> Finance. I put a suggested approver sequence in the sheet.

Deadline: please provide initial comments by EOD Monday (2027-12-13) so we can lock the pilot bands for recruiting early next week.

Notes in the sheet: I added a sample conversion for Global Band 4 -> UK/DE/FR local bands and a conservative rounding method (+/- 250 GBP / +/- 300 EUR). MarketScout (cc'd) validated the 50th/65th percentile references in the packet. TalentEdge (cc'd) can consult on local market nuances if we need bespoke adjustments for high-cost cities.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Head of Talent Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Salary scale translation and localization rules — global bands -> local offers

Rachel — thanks for pulling this together, useful start. A few quick points from comp/total rewards perspective:

- Keep base salary denominated in local currency; do not attempt to maintain global USD anchors when presenting offers. Candidates expect local currency.
- For mapping methodology: prefer an explicit percentile mapping (e.g., Global midpoint -> local 50th, Global upper quartile -> local 75th). Please add a column showing the percentile target used for conversion.
- Rounding: use currency-specific rounding (GBP to nearest 250, EUR to nearest 200, SEK to nearest 500). That prevents awkward midpoints.
- Benefits/OTE: call out which allowances (relocation, equity vesting schedule) remain global and which are localized.

Only open question: for London and Zurich do we add a fixed city factor or treat them through published market percentiles? My preference is to apply a +8% city uplift for Zurich and +6% for London, but I'd like validation from MarketScout.

If MarketScout confirms, I'm fine with the workflow as drafted.

Laura Bennett
VP, Total Rewards
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben@talentedge.co
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Salary scale translation and localization rules — global bands -> local offers

Looping in a quick conversion excerpt from the attached v2 sheet so we have something concrete for Monday's pilot:

- Rule: Global Band Midpoint (USD) -> Local Market Median (50th) using MarketScout local median values; apply currency conversion using monthly FX (set to 2027-11 average).
- Example (Gbl Band 4): Global midpoint = $140k -> UK median = 88k GBP -> rounded to nearest 250 GBP = 87,750 GBP (offer band lower bound 80k, midpoint 87,750, upper bound 95k).
- Percentile mapping: Midpoint -> 50th, Top quartile -> 75th.
- City uplift: apply only if MarketScout local median is below published city median by >6%; otherwise use percentile approach.

Benchmarks used: MarketScout EMEA median (attached) + local JobPost cadence (TalentEdge provided). For transparency I added a column for the FX rate and the source (cell comments in the sheet).

Action: if we agree, I'll lock the conversion rules and push the sheet to the recruiting template. Also propose a single-statement approval email (People Partner confirms regional band; Comp Lead signs) — reduces friction for high-velocity hires.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Compensation Strategy

Thanks — flagged two operational items after walking through the sheet: 

1) Recruiting templates: need separate templates for contractor vs. employee offers (one-sheet mapping). I'll create those once we lock the conversion rules.
2) APAC uplift: our APAC markets (SG/HK/SYD) historically run 5–12% higher vs. MarketScout medians for senior ICs; recommend a regional uplift table rather than per-country manual edits.

I created JIRA ticket HR-4789 to track the Workday changes and linked the proposed templates in the ticket. Also asked Finance to confirm budget tolerances for the first quarter pilot.

Forwarding Karthik's example (he included the conversion snippet above).
